thread.title: Nasdaq, Small Caps Slammed As Yield Curve Flattens | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Nasdaq, Small Caps Slammed As Yield Curve Flattens | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Russell 2000 showed a mean sell-off in the small-cap sector, and big-cap techs failed to avoid a sell-off in stocks today amid renewed concerns over interest rates.
X Just one day after stocks rallied on hopes that bilateral tariffs on imports between China and the U.S. will not increase, Wall Street sold equities hard as one portion of the U.S. Treasury yield curve showed a slight inversion. Specifically, the yield that an investor could now get by buying the 5-year Treasury bond is now less than what could be gotten by buying the shorter-term 2-year note.
Meanwhile, yield spreads have certainly tightened between short- and long-duration bonds.
While the 3-month Treasury bill delivers a 2.41% yield, the yield on the benchmark 10-year bond has fallen sharply in recent days and hit 2.90%, the lowest level since Sept. 6.
A severe inversion of the Treasury yield curve would increase the risk of an economic recession, economic observers say. For now, though, the U.S. economy has shown steady growth in wages, jobs, manufacturing activity and retail sales throughout the year. Read this Investor's Corner that details IBD research on how the stock market reacted to yield curve inversions (between 2-year and 10-year bonds) in the past.
The Russell 2000 paced the broad decline, sinking more than 3%, while the Nasdaq composite lost more than 3.2%. On Monday, the Nasdaq advanced 1.5% following a 5.6% rally last week.
A Big Challenge For The Nasdaq Notice on a daily chat how the Nasdaq is having a hard time reclaiming the 50-day moving average, a key support and resistance level. In a strong bull market, major equity indexes tend to rise above and lead their 50-day moving averages higher.
The Dow Jones industrial average and the S&P 500 both fell around 2.7%. In the 30-stock Dow, Caterpillar ( CAT ), Apple ( AAPL ), UnitedHealth ( UNH ) and Goldman Sachs ( GS ) were among 13 stocks to fall 3 points or more.
Verizon ( VZ ) and McDonald's ( MCD ) bucked the decline with small gains. Both stocks are on IBD Leaderboard and have rallied past proper breakout points.
Apple, which fell more than 3% to 177.92 in mild turnover, continues to seek a near-term bottom after getting as low as 170.26 last month. The iPhone, MacBook and Apple Watch maker continues to swim well beneath its 50- and 200-day lines. Ditto for Goldman Sachs, still reeling from a scandal with a major Malaysian investment fund. Shares in the Wall Street firm slid more than 2% to 185.83 and are now 32% below a 52-week peak of 275.31.
Goldman is down 27% since Jan. 1.
Volume continues to fall vs. the same time on Monday on both main exchanges. But market breadth worsened fast vs. Monday. Losers beat winners by a nearly 4-1 margin on both the NYSE and the Nasdaq.
Bank Stocks Lead Drop Among IBD's 197 industry groups, cyclicals and financials fell especially hard. RV makers slid 8% as a group.
Airfreight, truck transport, logistics, wood products, mortgage service, West and Southwest lender and superregional bank stocks slumped 4% or more. On the upside, auto parts retail, gold mining, electric utility and diversified utility stocks were the only groups among the 197 tracked each day by IBD to defy the sell-off.
See the entire daily performance and six-month relative price performance rankings of all 197 industry groups by going to IBD Data Tables in the Stock Lists section of Investors.com, then click on Industry Group Rankings.
A large number of lenders have had a tough time recovering ground lost in recent months. M&T Bank ( MTB ), SunTrust ( STI ) and Regions Financial ( RF ) fell 4% to 6% each. M&T undercut its 50-day moving average to extend its nine-month long downtrend. Shares trade 18% off a 197.37 52-week peak.
JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) fell nearly 5%. But at 107.23, the megacap financial institution trades just 10% below a 119.33 high. Shares are building a new base. It closed above the 50- and 200-day moving averages on Monday.
